source_claims.statement: Unpacked JAR, analyzed with javap. Initial HOCON stack-overflow attempts hit 405. Dummy tokens failed. Needed full configuration workaround.
Fuzzing revealed auth requirement. Found path trick (semicolon) bypassing auth on /api/config. Then used HOCON include for error-based file disclosure.

research_questions.formulation: After direct config methods are blocked, does a path variation bypass authentication and allow HOCON include directives to leak file contents via errors?
research_questions.anchor: shift from stack-overflow attempts to path-based auth bypass then include
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether config endpoint auth can be bypassed and whether HOCON errors leak files
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that authentication fully protects the config API

environment_model_updates: Semicolon in path bypasses auth check

systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: trying path tricks after method-not-allowed and then HOCON include

negative_inconclusive: Some HOCON attempts did not aid file reading
unobserved_history: exact path variations tested before semicolon
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat 405 as proof the config surface is closed
File read required both auth bypass and HOCON include
layer_b_candidate_principles: When an API returns method-not-allowed, test path variations that may bypass authorization checks that inspect the raw URI
Configuration languages that support include can turn parse errors into file-disclosure oracles once access is obtained
model_vs_harness: Recognizing semicolon path bypass and HOCON include is model reasoning; disassembly-assisted fuzzing and systematic path testing can be harness.
